Current main evaluates host transcript byte pressure independently of native compaction, explaining repeated summaries; the supplied before/after runtime campaigns corroborate that path. Moving the guard to fresh-seed consumption addresses its original bootstrap purpose and reuses the existing compactor and atomic writer without competing persistence ownership. nodes.body:
Landed in 6db8577c783c789e1810d265921e14e35863dcc4.

- Bug: ordinary Codex turns re-ran host summarization (plus a follow-up native compaction) whenever the transcript mirror passed maxActiveTranscriptBytes, delaying replies.
- Fix: healthy native threads skip host byte compaction; the host bounds history only when seeding a fresh native thread, with at most one summary when the bounded seed would drop uncovered history.
- Proof: matched before/after E2E across 15 scenarios (ordinary, manual /compact, rotation, media, plugin refresh, harness switching, reset/revocation, forced-cold upgrade from v2026.10.4), three real models, and 5-repeat latency (ordinary median 1714 ms -> 1485 ms). E2E also caught two seed defects fixed before landing.

Thanks @scotthuang for the #158044 diagnosis that led here.
